wu: Students play 'Quiz Quiz Trade' with KET-style flashcards. Each student gets a card with a question (e.g., 'What time do you get up?'). They walk around, ask their question, trade cards, and repeat with a new partner.
wuAlt: Students play 'Find Someone Who...' with a semester review grid (e.g., 'Find someone who likes football').
Students play 'Memory Race' with vocabulary cards from S1 topics.
pres: Teacher presents a KET speaking task rubric. Model a paired dialogue using flashcards of hobbies and locations. Ask students to identify the key phrases (e.g., 'I like...', 'Can you...?'). Check understanding with thumbs up/down.
presAlt: Teacher uses a short video of a KET speaking task to model.
Teacher presents a 'good vs bad' speaking example with exaggerated errors.
prac: Students practice the paired speaking task in groups of three. One student acts as the examiner, one as Candidate A, one as Candidate B. Teacher circulates and provides feedback on fluency and task completion.
pracAlt: Students play 'Role Card Relay'—draw a role card and act out the scenario with a partner.
Students complete a 'dialogue gap-fill' worksheet for the speaking task.
ls: Students listen to a KET-style listening track about daily routines. They complete a multiple-choice worksheet with 5 questions. Play the track twice, then review answers as a class.
re: Students play 'Simon Says' with action verbs from S1 (e.g., 'Simon says stand up', 'Simon says eat'). After the break, this reactivates energy and reviews vocabulary.
prod: Students work in pairs to create a short dialogue (5-6 turns) about their weekend plans using 'going to' and 'will'. They perform for the class and receive peer feedback.
rw: Students read a short text (50 words) about a Moroccan festival (e.g., Green March). They answer 3 multiple-choice questions and write 2 sentences about their own favorite festival.
st: Teacher tells a story about a student preparing for the KET exam. Close with: 'Today we reviewed for the semester quiz—thank you, class!'
g: Students mark off KET vocabulary words on a bingo card as the teacher calls them.
Students draw S1 vocabulary words for their team to guess.
Teams answer KET-style questions for points.
Students add one sentence to a story about their semester.
Students interview partners about their hobbies using KET prompts.
diff: Fast finishers: Write a 40-word paragraph about their best friend using comparatives.
Support learners: Use a sentence starter worksheet for the writing task.
hw: Review your S1 notes and write 5 sentences about your learning progress.
Create a flashcard set of 10 KET words you find difficult.
Do a 10-minute listening practice from the KET sample papers.
tip: Use peer assessment during the speaking task to build confidence and mimic the exam format—teens respond well to structured feedback from classmates.
checklist: I can answer personal information questions in the speaking task.
I can understand short conversations about daily routines.
I can read a short text and answer multiple-choice questions.
I can write 7-8 sentences about my weekend plans.
I can use present simple and past simple correctly.
I can follow a KET-style speaking task with a partner.
